brief.question: How was ether anaesthesia first used in surgery?
brief.purpose: The village surgeon in my 1850s mystery needs a believable way to put a patient under.

scope.name: Dr Ambrose Hale
scope.summary: A country surgeon who distrusts new methods.

stored.want: To keep his patients alive through the winter.

web.title: The first public ether operation
web.text: On 16 October 1846 the dentist William Morton gave ether to a patient at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston. The surgeon John Collins Warren then removed a tumour from the patient's neck while the patient slept. News of the ether demonstration reached British surgeons within two months.

web.title: Early anaesthesia in Britain
web.text: By 1847 many British surgeons used ether or chloroform for amputations. Chloroform was introduced by James Young Simpson in Edinburgh in November 1847. Country surgeons often preferred chloroform because it needed less equipment.

web.title: Manning a hawk
web.text: Medieval falconers began training by manning the bird, keeping it on the fist for many hours so it grew used to people. A hood made of leather kept the falcon calm in the dark. Falconers rewarded the bird with small pieces of meat on a lure.

web.title: The Pony Express
web.text: The Pony Express ran from April 1860 to October 1861 between Missouri and California. Riders changed horses at relay stations about every ten to fifteen miles. The mail crossed nearly two thousand miles in about ten days.
